# Resource: stripe_treasury_inbound_transfer

A transfer of money into a Treasury financial account from a US bank account attached to the connected account itself, which `origin_payment_method` names. Treasury runs on a platform's connected accounts, so manage inbound transfers through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is the connected account. The financial account needs its `inbound_transfers.ach` feature active. The provider does not attach the bank account: attach it in the Dashboard, or with a setup intent on the connected account that sets `attach_to_self` and `flow_directions = ["inbound"]`. Stripe refuses that setup intent on a Custom or Express connected account to platforms it considers new ("Creating direct charges with type=express or type=custom is not supported for new platforms"), and links migration and exemption instructions in the platform's Dashboard, so such a platform may be unable to make an inbound transfer. Set `status` to `canceled` to cancel a transfer that is still `processing`. Stripe refuses to cancel one that has succeeded or failed, so a plan that sets `canceled` then fails. Nothing else changes after creation.

~> A treasury inbound transfer can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one, including setting its `status`, fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete an inbound transfer; set `status` to `canceled` to cancel one that is still processing. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the treasury inbound transfer, fail at plan time. To stop managing a treasury inbound transfer, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "treasury_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "A connected account with the treasury capability active."
}

variable "financial_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "A financial account of the connected account."
}

# Treasury runs on a connected account, so a second provider configuration acts on it.
provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "treasury"
  stripe_account = var.treasury_account
}

variable "bank_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "A US bank account payment method attached to the connected account itself for inbound flows, by the Dashboard or a setup intent with attach_to_self."
}

resource "stripe_treasury_inbound_transfer" "top_up" {
  provider              = stripe.treasury
  financial_account     = var.financial_account
  amount                = 10000
  currency              = "usd"
  origin_payment_method = var.bank_account
  description           = "Weekly top-up"
}

# Set status = "canceled" to cancel the transfer while it is still processing.
output "inbound_status" {
  value = stripe_treasury_inbound_transfer.top_up.status
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `amount` - (Required) Amount (in cents) to be transferred. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `financial_account` - (Required) The FinancialAccount to send funds to. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `origin_payment_method` - (Required) The origin payment method to be debited for the InboundTransfer. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.

The following arguments are optional:

* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `statement_descriptor` - (Optional) The complete description that appears on your customers' statements. Maximum 10 characters. Can only include -#.$&*, spaces, and alphanumeric characters. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `status` - (Optional) Status of the InboundTransfer: `processing`, `succeeded`, `failed`, and `canceled`. An InboundTransfer is `processing` if it is created and pending. The status changes to `succeeded` once the funds have been "confirmed" and a `transaction` is created and posted. The status changes to `failed` if the transfer fails. Possible values: `canceled`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `cancelable` - Returns `true` if the InboundTransfer is able to be canceled.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `failure_details` - Details about this InboundTransfer's failure. Will be set when `status=failed` or `returned=true`. See [`failure_details`](#failure_details) below.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `linked_flows` - See [`linked_flows`](#linked_flows) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `origin_payment_method_details` - Details about the PaymentMethod for an InboundTransfer. See [`origin_payment_method_details`](#origin_payment_method_details) below.
* `returned` - Returns `true` if the funds for an InboundTransfer were returned after the InboundTransfer went to the `succeeded` state.
* `status_transitions` - See [`status_transitions`](#status_transitions) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="failure_details"></a>
### `failure_details`

The `failure_details` attribute supports:

* `code` - Reason for the failure. Possible values: `account_closed`, `account_frozen`, `bank_account_restricted`, `bank_ownership_changed`, `debit_not_authorized`, `incorrect_account_holder_address`, `incorrect_account_holder_name`, `incorrect_account_holder_tax_id`, `insufficient_funds`, `invalid_account_number`, `invalid_currency`, `no_account`, `other`.

<a id="linked_flows"></a>
### `linked_flows`

The `linked_flows` attribute supports:

* `received_debit` - If funds for this flow were returned after the flow went to the `succeeded` state, this field contains a reference to the ReceivedDebit return.

<a id="origin_payment_method_details"></a>
### `origin_payment_method_details`

The `origin_payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `billing_details` - See [`origin_payment_method_details.billing_details`](#origin_payment_method_details.billing_details) below.
* `type` - The type of the payment method used in the InboundTransfer. Possible values: `us_bank_account`.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="origin_payment_method_details.billing_details"></a>
### `origin_payment_method_details.billing_details`

The `origin_payment_method_details.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`origin_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`](#origin_payment_method_details.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.

<a id="origin_payment_method_details.billing_details.address"></a>
### `origin_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`

The `origin_payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Account holder type: individual or company. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - Account type: checkings or savings. Defaults to checking if omitted. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `network` - The network rails used. See the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/money-movement/timelines) to learn more about money movement timelines for each network type. Possible values: `ach`.
* `routing_number` - Routing number of the bank account.

<a id="status_transitions"></a>
### `status_transitions`

The `status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `canceled_at` - Timestamp describing when an InboundTransfer changed status to `canceled`.
* `failed_at` - Timestamp describing when an InboundTransfer changed status to `failed`.
* `succeeded_at` - Timestamp describing when an InboundTransfer changed status to `succeeded`.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a treasury inbound transfer whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_treasury_inbound_transfer.top_up

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_treasury_inbound_transfer.top_up
```

The treasury inbound transfer stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

Run the import where the resource's `provider` acts on the connected account that holds it.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a treasury inbound transfer using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_treasury_inbound_transfer.top_up
  id = "ibt_1MtWwWLkdIwHu7ixjwHBoXWD"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_treasury_inbound_transfer.top_up
  identity = {
    id = "ibt_1MtWwWLkdIwHu7ixjwHBoXWD"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the treasury inbound transfer.

Using `terraform import`, import a treasury inbound transfer using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_treasury_inbound_transfer.top_up ibt_1MtWwWLkdIwHu7ixjwHBoXWD
```
